ticket.title: Add a standalone-build gate: every member must build with no harness path patches, from published crates only
ticket.description:
Raised by the owner as a standing concern: 'individual tool use vs suite interoperability - both are important'. The layer gate protects interoperability (it forbids hidden coupling). NOTHING currently protects individual tool use, and the suite has already drifted: gaugeblock-workspace and gaugeblock-security are consumed by six member repositories and neither is published, so those members only build because the harness [patch.crates-io] table maps them to local paths. A checkout of sawhorse on its own cannot build. Measured 2026-11-06 against the crates.io API: of 51 package names, 5 are unpublished.\n\nShape: 'outfeed gate --standalone' (or miter) that, per member repository, resolves dependencies with the patch table disabled and fails when any dependency cannot be satisfied from the registry. It would have caught this drift the day the first unpublished dependency was introduced, and it is the guard that makes Law 2 (each repository compiles and is useful on its own) enforceable instead of aspirational. Cheapest implementation may be a cargo metadata pass with --offline and a temporary .cargo/config.toml that omits [patch.crates-io].

PARTIAL 2026-11-10 (outfeed 12cead4): the resolver and its classifier are in outfeed-core standalone.rs; the CLI verb and the chain wiring are not, and both are explained rather than forgotten. Landed: check_standalone resolves every suite member from a scratch directory OUTSIDE the suite with --manifest-path, because cargo reads .cargo/config.toml from the working directory upward - which is what makes the root patch.crates-io table inapplicable, and therefore what makes the check mean anything. Outcomes are Standalone / NeedsUnpublished{package} / Broken{detail}, with both spellings of an unpublished crate recognised and everything else left Broken, since excusing a parse error as waiting-on-a-publish is how a gate stops being one. Outstanding: the outfeed standalone verb - mechanical, deferred because its shape depends on how the chain consumes it - and wiring it into a chain, which must wait until publishing makes it green, because a gate that is red for every member on day one is one everybody learns to skip. RELATED GAP THIS SPLIT EXPOSED: this resolves, it does not compile, so it would not have caught SP-41 - which added three contract fields, compiled inside storypole, and broke joiner-core and a benchwork-core test for ten tickets until an unrelated build tripped over them. That is a different gate and is filed separately rather than conflated here.
